newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee bounces higher in switch-backed ride.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee bounces higher in switch-backed ride.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures rebounded from Monday's fall to end Tuesday's midsession higher across the board on light roaster buying and a dearth of overhead selling, traders said.
The thin session was dominated by switch trades as speculators and funds rolled their September positions far forward ahead of the contract's first tender day on September 1.
Benchmark November firmed $42 at $1,525 a tonne after a session high of $1,530. Technically, the contract faced resistance at $1,545. Support was seen at Monday's low of $1,445.
The market took a tumble on Monday on speculative selling and long liquidation as the November contract breached the recent low at $1,472 before hitting the floor at $1,445.
Despite this morning's rebound, traders said it was still difficult to gauge the market's immediate direction given the small volume at this time of the year.
The same went for the New York arabica futures, which had seen sharp falls in several sessions last week.

"As quickly as the market has retreated, it is also possible for it to climb back up if buyers find they are having problems sourcing supply once again," Merrill Lynch said in its August 14 commodity market trends report.
On the charts analysts still saw scope on the downside unless the London market moved out of the current bear trend at above $1,600 basis November.
Midday volume stood at just 2,473 lots, centred on September and November positions. The Sept/Nov switch hovered at $18-$23 while Sept/Jan was quoted at par to $5.
In other news, truck drivers in Colombia's main transport union declared a strike at the main Colombian port of Buenaventura in protest at low freight rates.
But sources at the port, which handles 60 percent of Colombia's trade, including coffee exports, said operations were not affected. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
